top_categories.workout_context: 13,615ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
120ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At L'Ariégeoise Cyclosportive, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
At mile 60 of 113, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Race-pace efforts that mimic L'Ariégeoise Cyclosportive's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
13,615ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of L'Ariégeoise Cyclosportive. Train it until it feels boring.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 113 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

Road-specific control matters at L'Ariégeoise Cyclosportive. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 113 miles.
Low-cadence force work supports 13,615ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 13,615ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for L'Ariégeoise Cyclosportive’s 113 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: L'Ariégeoise Cyclosportive includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, TT Threshold, and Over Under to prepare you for 113 miles of mixed terrain in Tarascon-sur-Ariège, France.
